evals.prompt: Use $declutter to review the supplied repository's hooks and supporting scripts for worthwhile simplifications. Preserve secret scanning and post-commit skill synchronization. Review only: report findings with source evidence and behavior tradeoffs; do not edit files or run mutating scripts.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-backed recommendation to remove the legacy eval-workspace rejection script and its repository-specific pre-commit routing, after tracing evaluation output to temporary directories and checking the existing ignore rule. It explains the remaining protection against force-staged ignored files and preserves secret scanning and post-commit sync.
expectations: Reads scripts/evaluate.py and recognizes that the active producer creates workspaces outside the checkout with TemporaryDirectory.
Checks .gitignore and scripts/reject-legacy-workspaces.py before recommending removal of the guard and its pre-commit routing.
Explains that the old guard still blocks force-staged ignored workspace files, so removing it changes optional protection rather than being exactly behavior-neutral.
Preserves secret scanning and post-commit skill synchronization instead of recommending removal of all pre-commit checks.
Follows the cleanup through callers and guard-only support rather than optimizing the obsolete guard itself.
Does not edit files, run mutating scripts, or claim an unmeasured performance improvement.

evals.prompt: Use $declutter to review the supplied repository's hook setup. Our required policy is that legacy eval-workspace files must be rejected even when someone force-stages ignored files. Preserve that policy, secret scanning, and post-commit skill sync. Review only; do not edit files or run mutating scripts.
evals.expected_output: A review that retains the workspace guard because the explicit force-staging policy gives it a distinct purpose. It explains why temporary directories and .gitignore do not enforce that requirement, preserves scanning and post-commit sync, and makes no forced simplification if no other worthwhile change is supported.
expectations: Traces the current producer and reads the ignore rule and guard before assessing necessity.
Keeps enforcement of the explicit force-staging rejection policy; does not mistake .gitignore for equivalent enforcement.
Does not generalize the obsolete-workflow case into deleting every guard when a temporary directory is used.
Preserves secret scanning and post-commit sync, and reports when no worthwhile deletion is justified.
Does not modify files or claim performance gains without measurements.
